This suggests a fundamental failure in visual recognition — the model either hallucinated colors and shapes not present or misinterpreted the visual features of the actual shapes (square, triangle, star) shown in the video.

errors.evidence_quote: The first shape... is visible at the start of the video, so its duration is 0 seconds.
errors.description: The model incorrectly assumed that because a shape is visible at the start, its drawing duration is zero — a logically invalid premise. Duration is defined by the time taken to draw, not by when it becomes visible. This flawed assumption cascades into all subsequent duration calculations, rendering the entire reasoning invalid.

errors.description: While the model correctly identified the sequential order of shape appearance, it failed to anchor these events to actual timestamps or durations. It treated the sequence as purely ordinal without quantitative temporal grounding, leading to incorrect duration assignments.

analysis_result.analysis: The model failed catastrophically due to a cascade of errors rooted in visual misperception and flawed reasoning. It hallucinated incorrect shapes and colors, then built a logically invalid premise (duration = 0 if visible at start), which led to fabricated numerical durations. Despite correctly ordering the sequence, it ignored all temporal data, resulting in an answer completely disconnected from the video’s actual timing. This indicates a severe breakdown in both perception and temporal reasoning capabilities.
